questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Italy?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Italy article.

questions.proof: The country's capital, Rome, is one of the most famous cities in the world.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Italy?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “People and culture” part of the Italy article.

questions.proof: The official language of Italy is Italian.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Italy gained the Trentino and South Tyrol, which had been part of _____.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “part”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Kingdom of Italy” part of the Italy article.

questions.proof: Italy gained the Trentino and South Tyrol, which had been part of Austria.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “_____, Japan, and Italy entered the Axis powers.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Japan”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Fascist Italy” part of the Italy article.

questions.proof: Germany, Japan, and Italy entered the Axis powers.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Italy started fighting as an ally of _____ and the United Kingdom, but Italian soldiers did not know whom to shoot.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “ally”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Fascist Italy” part of the Italy article.

questions.proof: Italy started fighting as an ally of France and the United Kingdom, but Italian soldiers did not know whom to shoot.
